text: Two studies show non-coding 3'UTRs modulate microRNA function. Versican 3'UTR antagonizes and lowers miR-199a-3p levels in mouse breast carcinoma 4T1 cells; miR-199a-3p and miR-144 target cell-cycle regulator Rb1, while miR-144 and miR-136 target PTEN. The 3'UTR bound these miRNAs, freeing Rb1 and PTEN mRNAs for translation, up-regulating them synergistically in vitro and in vivo. Cells transfected with the 3'UTR formed smaller tumors than controls, implicating miRNA degradation in tumorigenesis. Separately, the ~1.7 kb spliced, highly abundant murine cytomegalovirus m169 transcript mediates rapid degradation of cellular miR-27a/b during lytic infection, via a single optimized miRNA binding site in its 3'-UTR. Expressing only the m169 3'-UTR from an adenoviral vector sufficed; degradation involved 3'-tailing and -trimming and was mutual. Three mutant viruses unable to target miR-27a/b lost efficiency in vivo.
